questions.question: Explain the purpose of a trial balance. Classify each as a debit or credit balance: bank, equipment, drawings, wages, capital, loan, current income, rent income. Give two errors that would not be revealed by the trial balance.
questions.expected_answer: A trial balance lists all ledger balances on a date to check the arithmetical accuracy of the double entry: total debits must equal total credits. Debit: bank, equipment, drawings, wages. Credit: capital, loan, current income, rent income. Errors not revealed: omission of a whole transaction; posting to the wrong account on the correct side (commission); error of principle (equipment recorded as an expense); wrong amount entered on both sides (original entry); compensating errors.

questions.question: From these balances prepare a summary income statement for March: current income R15 900, rent income R2 500, interest income R150, wages R6 000, stationery R750, water and electricity R1 400, bank charges R220. Name three trial balance items that do not appear on it and why.
questions.expected_answer: Income: 15 900 + 2 500 + 150 = R18 550. Expenses: 6 000 + 750 + 1 400 + 220 = R8 370. Net profit = R10 180. Not included: equipment (an asset — balance sheet); capital and loan (sources of finance, not income — balance sheet); drawings (a withdrawal by the owner, not an expense — reduces owner's equity on the balance sheet).

questions.question: Prepare a summary balance sheet at 31 March: equipment R18 000, bank R74 180, capital R60 000, drawings R3 000, loan R25 000, net profit R10 180. Explain why the balance sheet heading shows a date and how net profit links the two statements.
questions.expected_answer: Assets: non-current — equipment R18 000; current — bank R74 180; total R92 180. Owner's equity = 60 000 + 10 180 − 3 000 = R67 180; non-current liability — loan R25 000; total R92 180. The balance sheet is a snapshot of the financial position at one moment, so it shows a single date. Net profit is calculated on the income statement for the period and added to capital in owner's equity on the balance sheet.
